items.s: Who must register with DIR, what it costs, when it renews, and what happens if you work unregistered.
items.x: In one sentence: every contractor and subcontractor on a public works job over the thresholds must hold a current DIR public works contractor registration, from the moment it bids until its last day of work. Who must register Any contractor or subcontractor that bids on or performs public works on a construction project over $25,000 or a maintenance project over $15,000 . Registration is with the Department of Industrial Relations, through its online public works portal. It is separate from your CSLB license. What it takes To register you certify that you: carry workers' compensation coverage for any employees, and use only registered subcontractors; hold a CSLB license if your trade requires one; have no delinquent unpaid wage or penalty assessments; are not debarred under state or federal law. What it costs and when it renews As of November 2026, DIR's page lists $400 for one fiscal year, $800 for two and $1,200 for three . The registration year runs July 1 to June 30 . Late renewal carries a penalty, and working or bidding while unregistered carries larger ones, so put the renewal date on the company calendar. The registration number You'll write it on your bid, on your subcontractor list (for each sub) and on certified payroll. Agencies may not accept a bid or sign a contract or subcontract without proof of current registration. The project side The awarding body registers the project with DIR (form PWC 100) after award. That record is what your certified payroll is filed against. If you can't find the project in DIR's system, ask the agency: it is their filing. See certified payroll. If a sub isn't registered The prime can be penalized for using an unregistered sub, and the sub can't lawfully work on the job. Check registration on DIR's public search before the sub mobilizes, and again after July 1 each year.

items.s: How bid, performance and payment bonds work, what a surety looks at, and how bonding capacity limits what you can bid.
items.x: In one sentence: a bond is the surety's promise to the agency that you will do what you said, and your bonding capacity, not your ambition, decides how big a job you can bid. A bond is not insurance A bond has three parties: you (the principal ), the agency (the obligee ) and the surety . If the surety pays a claim, it comes back to you for the money, usually through the indemnity agreement the company owners signed. Insurance protects you; a bond protects the agency and the people you owe. The three bonds you'll meet Bid bond: guarantees you'll sign the contract and provide the other bonds if you're the winning bidder. Usually 10% of the bid. See bid security. Performance bond: guarantees the work gets done, usually 100% of the contract price. Payment bond: guarantees your subs, suppliers and workers get paid, 100% of the contract price, required on public works over $25,000. See payment performance bonds. What a surety looks at Character: history, references, how claims were handled. Capacity: experience with work of this kind and size, key people, equipment. Capital: financial statements (reviewed or audited for larger programs), working capital, net worth, bank line. From this the surety sets two limits: a single job limit and an aggregate limit (all bonded work on hand, usually measured on the uncompleted portion). The cost Premium is a percentage of the contract amount, on a sliding scale that gets cheaper per dollar for larger contracts and stronger contractors. Bid bonds are usually free to good clients; the premium comes with the performance and payment bonds after award. Change orders that raise the contract usually raise the premium too. Small contractors If you're new, look for a surety agent who works with small contractors. California also has programs that help small and disadvantaged firms qualify for bonds. Start the relationship months before the bid you care about.

items.s: The coverages public agencies ask for, the endorsements that trip contractors up, and how to read the insurance section of the contract.
items.x: In one sentence: the contract's insurance section lists coverages, limits and endorsements; send it to your broker before you bid, because a missing endorsement can hold up the contract signature. Coverages you'll be asked for Commercial general liability (CGL): per occurrence and aggregate limits, often with completed operations. Commercial auto liability: owned, hired and non owned vehicles. Workers' compensation at statutory limits, plus employer's liability. Umbrella or excess liability on larger jobs to reach the required total. Sometimes: pollution liability, professional liability (design build), builder's risk, railroad protective liability near tracks. Endorsements that matter Additional insured: the agency (and often its officers, employees and consultants) named as additional insured on your CGL and auto policies, including completed operations. Primary and non contributory: your policy pays first, without asking the agency's insurance to share. Waiver of subrogation: your insurer gives up the right to recover from the agency. Notice of cancellation: advance notice to the agency. Many agencies want copies of the endorsements themselves, not just the certificate of insurance. Subcontractors The contract usually requires you to pass the same requirements down to subs, sometimes with lower limits. Collect their certificates and endorsements before they mobilize. PM notes Keep a one page summary of each job's insurance requirements in the job file, with expiration dates. Certificates expire during long jobs, and some agencies hold payment until a current one is on file.

items.s: Where California agencies advertise their work, how to follow a bid, and how to decide which ones are worth your time.
items.x: In one sentence: public bids are advertised in public, but across hundreds of agency sites; the work is in finding the few that fit your license, size, location and crew. Where agencies advertise Caltrans: its own contract advertisement pages, district by district. See bid package for what a Caltrans package contains. Local agencies: their own websites or bid platforms (several cities and counties share commercial platforms), plus legal notices in a newspaper of general circulation. Builders' exchanges and plan rooms: regional services that collect notices and plans. State procurement: the state's eProcurement system, Cal eProcure, for some state departments and for Caltrans Minor B jobs under $461,000. See caltrans contract types. Primes looking for subs: if you're a sub, primes advertise for quotes, often with DBE or small business outreach. Following a bid Register as a plan holder. It's how you receive addenda, and some agencies only accept bids from registered plan holders. Note the pre bid meeting (sometimes mandatory), the deadline for questions, and the bid opening date and place. Go or no go Before you spend a week on an estimate, check: 1. License class required, and the experience requirements if any. 2. Bond: does it fit your single job and aggregate limits? 3. Size and schedule: working days, liquidated damages, night work. 4. Location: travel and subsistence costs under the prevailing wage determination. 5. Self performed share: many contracts require the prime to do a minimum share of the work with its own forces. 6. Who else is bidding: the plan holders list tells you the competition. Bid results Agencies publish bid results after opening. Reading them shows who wins what, at which prices, and where your numbers stand.

items.t: Caltrans contract types: Major, Minor A and Minor B
items.s: How Caltrans sorts construction contracts by size, where each kind is advertised, and why Minor B jobs are reserved for small businesses.
items.x: In one sentence: Caltrans sorts construction contracts by size into Major , Minor A and Minor B , and the tier decides where the job is advertised, who can bid it as prime and how it is paid. The three tiers Tier Size (as of November 2026) Advertised on Who can bid as prime Major Above the Minor A limit Contractor's Corner Any qualified contractor Minor A Up to about $1.25 million Contractor's Corner Any qualified contractor Minor B Under $461,000 Cal eProcure Certified small businesses (limited exceptions) The limits are not fixed. The Minor B limit follows the lower limit of the State Contract Act and is reviewed every two years, which is why older pages show $333,000 or $388,000. Check the current figure on Caltrans' Contractor's Corner before you rely on it. Where the money comes from Minor A and Minor B jobs are funded by the SHOPP Minor Program , the part of the State Highway Operation and Protection Program set aside for small repair, safety and operational projects. The California Transportation Commission approves the program, and Caltrans updates the Minor B project list during the year. Typical electrical Minor B work: detector loop replacement, signal and lighting repairs, conduit and pull box fixes, small CCTV or ramp meter upgrades. How Minor B is different Small business only. Since 2021, Caltrans has set aside Minor B public works contracts for certified small businesses (SB), with limited exceptions. You need California SB certification to bid as prime. The DVBE goal that applies elsewhere does not apply on SB Minor B contracts. Designed by the district. District Minor B staff prepare the plans, specifications and estimate and administer the contract through completion. The packages are shorter and simpler than a major job's. Advertised by DPAC, not Contractor's Corner. Caltrans' Division of Procurement and Contracts posts Minor B solicitations on Cal eProcure . Search the event name for "Minor B". Plan holder lists are not published on Contractor's Corner for Minor B, so you can't see the competition the same way. Bidder inquiries go through the district (some regions post the questions and answers on their own Caltrans page). Paid in arrears on invoice. There is no monthly progress estimate like on a major contract. You invoice, the work is received, and Caltrans must pay within 45 days of a proper invoice or owe interest. The contract manager can hold money for missing or wrong certified payrolls. See certified payroll. Prevailing wage, DIR registration and the other public works rules still apply to Minor B jobs. See prevailing wage. Why it matters to a small electrical contractor Minor B is the easiest way to become a Caltrans prime : small jobs, short schedules, a smaller bond, and you bid only against other small businesses. Winning a few builds the experience and bonding history you need for Minor A and major jobs. See surety bonding. If you look for bids only on Contractor's Corner, you will miss every Minor B job. Add Cal eProcure to the sources in finding public bids. PM notes Keep your SB certification current: it can expire, and an expired certification can make your bid nonresponsive. With no progress payments, a Minor B job is financed by you until the invoice is paid. Plan the cash before you bid. See progress payments retention. Read the bid documents for the exact limit and rules on each job: they govern over this page.

items.s: The bid form, unit prices, addenda and the forms that must come with the bid, and how to avoid a nonresponsive bid.
items.x: In one sentence: a public bid is judged first on whether it is responsive , meaning complete and exactly in the form asked, and only then on price. Read the instructions first The notice to bidders and the instructions to bidders say what's required, in what form and by when. Read them before the plans. Note the documents due with the bid and those due after opening (often within a set number of days). The bid form Unit price contracts (most highway work): you price each bid item per unit; the agency multiplies by its estimated quantities. Extensions and totals must add up. On most agencies' forms, if the extension and unit price disagree, the unit price governs . Lump sum contracts (many building jobs): one total, sometimes with alternates. Additive or deductive alternates: read how the agency will choose the low bidder; it is stated in the documents. Forms that usually go with the bid Bid security. See bid security. Subcontractor list. See subcontractor listing. Acknowledgement of every addendum. Non collusion declaration. Bidder's experience or qualifications, if asked. DIR registration and license numbers. On federal aid jobs, federal certifications and DBE forms as the special provisions require. See dbe requirements. Responsiveness and responsibility A bid is responsive when it follows the instructions. A bidder is responsible when it can do the work: license, experience, financial capacity, past performance. An agency can reject the low bid for either reason, but it must follow its own procedures and usually give the bidder a chance to respond. Before you seal it A second person checks: every addendum acknowledged, every signature, the bond amount against the bid total, the subcontractor list against the estimate, and the arithmetic.

items.t: Bid security: bid bonds and other forms
items.s: Why every public bid carries security, the usual 10% amount, and what happens if the low bidder refuses to sign.
items.x: In one sentence: bid security guarantees the agency that if you win, you'll sign the contract and deliver the bonds and insurance; if you don't, the agency keeps the security. Forms of bid security Bid bond from an admitted surety, the usual choice. Cashier's check or certified check payable to the agency. Cash , accepted by some agencies. The amount is set in the bid documents and is usually at least 10% of the total bid . Some agencies ask for 10% of the base bid plus alternates; read the instruction. After bid opening Losing bidders get their security back, usually after award or contract signature. The winning bidder's security is held until it signs the contract and delivers the performance bond, payment bond and insurance on time. If the winner fails to sign or bond within the time allowed, the agency can keep the security and award to the next bidder. Mistakes in the bid A bidder that made a clerical mistake can ask to be relieved of its bid without losing the security, but the conditions are strict. Under Public Contract Code 5103 it must give written notice within five working days after opening, describing how the mistake happened, and the mistake must be in filling out the bid, not an error in judgment. See bid opening award protests. PM notes When the bid total changes in the last hour, check that the bond amount still covers 10% of the new total, or that the bond is written as "10% of the amount bid".

items.s: The Subletting and Subcontracting Fair Practices Act: who must be listed, what to write, and when a listed sub can be replaced.
items.x: In one sentence: a prime bidding California public works must list in its bid every sub that will do more than a set share of the work, and then use those subs, unless the agency approves a substitution for a reason the law allows. The threshold Under Public Contract Code 4104, you list each subcontractor whose work is more than one half of 1% of your total bid . For streets, highways and bridges, the threshold is one half of 1% or $10,000, whichever is greater . A specialty sub that fabricates and installs to detailed drawings is listed the same way. What to write for each sub Name and location of its place of business. California contractor license number. DIR public works contractor registration number. The portion of the work it will do. List only one sub per portion. An inadvertent error in a license or registration number can be fixed within 24 hours after bid opening. Other errors are harder to fix. If you don't list a sub For a portion above the threshold with no sub listed, the law treats you as agreeing to do that work yourself, and you can't sublet it later except under the substitution rules. Substitution after award You can't replace a listed sub on your own. The agency may consent to a substitution in the situations Public Contract Code 4107 allows, for example when the listed sub: refuses to sign a written contract at its bid price and scope; goes bankrupt or out of business; can't perform or can't provide a bond you required in advance; is not licensed or registered as required. The sub gets notice and the chance to object, and the agency decides. DBE commitments are separate On federal aid jobs, the DBE commitment form is a different document from the subcontractor list, with its own rules for replacing a DBE. See dbe requirements.

items.s: What the Disadvantaged Business Enterprise program asks of contractors, and how it changed with the 2025 federal rule.
items.x: In one sentence: on jobs paid with federal transportation money, the DBE program under 49 CFR Part 26 sets rules for using certified disadvantaged businesses, and in late 2026 it is in transition, so read each job's special provisions. The program The U.S. Department of Transportation's DBE program applies to contracts funded in part by federal highway, transit and airport money. Caltrans and local agencies spending those funds run it in California. A DBE is a small business certified through the California Unified Certification Program. What changed in 2025–2026 In October 2025 , USDOT issued an Interim Final Rule that substantially revised 49 CFR Part 26, and certified firms are being re evaluated. Caltrans' local assistance bulletin of August 2026 states that DBE contract goals and goal based monitoring remain suspended until the re evaluations are complete and FHWA accepts Caltrans' DBE Program Plan. Other parts of the program, notably prompt payment reporting, remain in force. What this means for you: on each federal aid bid, read the special provisions and any addenda for: whether the job has a DBE contract goal and what must be submitted with the bid or after; the forms in use (Caltrans has used a DBE commitment form and a good faith efforts form); the reporting required during the job. Rules that still matter during the job Prompt payment: pay subs within the time the contract sets (7 days after you're paid on Caltrans and local federal aid work, under state law) and report monthly when the contract asks. See prompt payment subcontractors. Commercially useful function: a DBE counts only for work it actually performs, manages and supervises with its own forces. Terminating or reducing a DBE's committed work needs the agency's written consent and a good cause reason, with notice to the DBE. PM notes Keep the DBE paperwork with the subcontract file, not only in the bid folder: it's the field and payment records that get reviewed during the job.

items.s: What happens at bid opening, how agencies pick the lowest responsive responsible bidder, bid protests, and relief for a bid mistake.
items.x: In one sentence: the lowest bid at opening is only the apparent low bid; the award goes to the lowest responsive bid from a responsible bidder, after any protests are resolved. Bid opening Bids are opened in public at the stated time. Late bids are returned unopened. The agency reads or posts the totals and later publishes the bid results with every bidder's amount, and for unit price jobs, every item price. Evaluation The agency checks the apparent low bid: Responsive: bid security, subcontractor list, addenda acknowledged, forms signed, arithmetic. A minor irregularity can be waived; a material one can't. Responsible: license, DIR registration, experience and past performance when the documents ask for them. Federal aid forms due after opening, on the days set in the special provisions. Protests A bidder that believes the low bid is nonresponsive, or that its own bid was wrongly rejected, can protest. The bid documents set the deadline (often a few business days after opening) and the form. Protests must be specific and in writing. The protested bidder gets a chance to respond, and the agency or its governing body decides before award. Bid mistakes A bidder can ask to be relieved of its bid for a mistake under Public Contract Code 5100–5110 if it can show that: 1. a mistake was made; 2. it gave written notice within five working days after opening, detailing how the mistake occurred; 3. the mistake made the bid materially different from what was intended; 4. the mistake was in filling out the bid, not an error in judgment or a careless reading of the plans. Award and signing After award, the contractor has a set number of days to sign the contract and deliver bonds and insurance. Missing that deadline can forfeit the bid security. Work starts only after the notice to proceed.

items.s: How to find the rate for each craft and county, what it includes, how fringe benefits count, and the overtime and travel rules.
items.x: In one sentence: every worker on public works must be paid at least the prevailing wage for the work they actually do, in the county where the job is, as published by DIR for the bid advertisement date. Finding the right rate DIR publishes prevailing wage determinations for each craft (inside wireman, laborer, operating engineer, and many more) by county. Use the determination in effect on the date the bid was advertised . Many determinations include predetermined increases on known dates, marked in the document; those apply during the job. Pay by the work performed , not by job title. A worker who pulls wire for half a day and digs trench the other half is paid each rate for those hours, and your payroll must show both. What the rate includes Basic hourly rate. Fringe benefits: health and welfare, pension, vacation and holiday, training, other. Overtime and holiday rates and the hours that trigger them. Travel and subsistence where the determination provides it. Training fund contributions for apprenticeable crafts. Fringe benefits: cash or plan You can pay fringe benefits into bona fide plans, as cash on the paycheck, or a mix, as long as the total meets the rate. Since January 1, 2026 (AB 889), California requires employers to annualize fringe benefit credits, so that a plan contribution counts only for the hours actually worked across all jobs, public and private, and to keep records that show it. Overtime The determination says when overtime applies: daily hours over 8, weekly over 40, Saturdays, Sundays, holidays and night shifts, depending on the craft. Failing to pay the prevailing overtime rate carries its own penalty. Changes coming For prime contracts of $35 million or more , AB 1198 will apply new determinations mid project from July 1, 2027 . Smaller contracts keep the rates fixed at advertisement, plus the predetermined increases. PM notes Print the determinations for every craft you might use on the job and keep them in the job file, with the advertisement date written on top. It is the first thing an auditor asks for.

items.s: What certified payroll records contain, how and when they are filed with DIR, and how to keep them audit-ready.
items.x: In one sentence: certified payroll is your weekly payroll for the job, worker by worker and day by day, signed under penalty of perjury and filed electronically with DIR. What a certified payroll record shows For each worker on the job, each week: name, address and last four digits of the Social Security number (follow the current form's rules); work classification, including apprentice status and step; hours worked each day and the total, straight time and overtime; rate paid, gross wages for the job and all jobs; fringe benefits paid as cash or to plans; deductions and net pay; a signed statement of compliance . Filing with DIR California requires contractors and subcontractors to submit certified payroll electronically to the Labor Commissioner through DIR's system, against the project the agency registered with the PWC 100. Submit at least monthly, or more often if the contract asks; many agencies also want copies weekly. Use a "no work performed" statement for weeks with no work on the job. Keeping records Keep the payroll records and the time records behind them for the period the law requires, and produce them when the agency, the Labor Commissioner or a joint labor management committee asks. From January 1, 2027 , a contractor that does not timely produce requested payroll records may be barred from using them later in its own defense (SB 1316). Federal aid jobs Federal aid jobs also use the federal weekly payroll form or an equivalent, submitted to the agency weekly under the FHWA 1273 provisions. See federal aid davis bacon. Who signs The contractor's owner or an authorized officer signs the statement of compliance. A false statement exposes the signer personally. PM notes Make the sub's certified payroll a condition of its pay application: no payroll, no payment. Check it against your daily reports headcount, which is what auditors do.

items.s: The DAS 140 and DAS 142 forms, the one-hour-in-five ratio, training fund contributions and the usual mistakes.
items.x: In one sentence: on contracts of $30,000 or more, each apprenticeable craft must send contract award information to apprenticeship programs, request apprentices, and employ at least one apprentice hour for every five journeyperson hours by the end of the job. When it applies All public works contracts of $30,000 or more carry the obligation, for each craft or trade that is apprenticeable under the prevailing wage determination. The obligation is per contractor and per craft. The steps 1. Notify (DAS 140). Before starting work, and within 10 days of signing the contract, send contract award information to the apprenticeship programs that can supply apprentices to the job, for each craft you will use. If you are not already approved to train, send it to every program in the area for that craft. 2. Request (DAS 142). When you need apprentices, ask the program to dispatch them, at least three business days before they are needed. 3. Employ in ratio. At least one hour of apprentice work for every five hours of journeyperson work, per craft, counting straight time hours, measured over the whole job. Apprentices must be registered in an approved program, paid the apprentice rate for their step, and supervised as the program requires. 4. Contribute to training funds for each apprenticeable craft, at the rate shown in the determination, to an approved program or the California Apprenticeship Council. Exemptions Some situations exempt a contractor or craft, for example a contract under $30,000, or an approved exemption from DAS. Keep the exemption letter in the job file. PM notes Plan the ratio from the start. It's easier to add an apprentice to a crew in month one than to make up the hours in the last week.

items.s: What changes when a California job is paid partly with federal highway money: two sets of wage rates, the required contract provisions and weekly payroll.
items.x: In one sentence: on a federal aid job you follow both the federal Davis Bacon rules and California prevailing wage law, and you pay whichever rate is higher for each craft. How to tell The contract says so: a federal aid project number, federal wage decisions bound into the special provisions, and the FHWA 1273 "Required Contract Provisions" attached. FHWA 1273 must be included, word for word, in every subcontract too. Two sets of rates Federal wage decision (Davis Bacon), published for the county and type of construction, included in the bid documents. California prevailing wage determination from DIR. For each classification, pay the higher of the two, including fringe benefits, and make sure the classification exists in both or is properly matched. What FHWA 1273 adds Nondiscrimination and equal employment opportunity requirements. Davis Bacon wage and payroll requirements, with weekly submission of certified payroll to the agency. Posting of wage rates and notices on the job site. Rules against convict labor, kickbacks and false statements. Subcontracting limits: the prime usually must perform a minimum share of the work (often 30%) with its own forces. Safety and health requirements. Payroll Weekly certified payroll on the federal form or an equivalent with the same information, to the agency, plus California's electronic filing with DIR. One payroll system can serve both if it captures everything. Other federal pieces Buy America: steel, iron and, increasingly, manufactured products must be produced in the United States unless a waiver applies. Material certificates matter. DBE: see dbe requirements. Interviews: the agency may interview workers on site to check wages. PM notes Federal aid labor compliance is reviewed during the job, not only at the end. Treat the weekly payroll as a deliverable like a submittal.

items.s: How the Labor Commissioner and agencies enforce prevailing wage and apprenticeship rules, and what the penalties look like.
items.x: In one sentence: prevailing wage violations cost back wages plus per worker, per day penalties that add up fast, and the prime can be held responsible for its subs. Who enforces The awarding agency reviews certified payroll and may withhold payments when records are missing or wrong. The Labor Commissioner's Office investigates complaints and reviews projects, and can issue a civil wage and penalty assessment against the contractor and its subs. Joint labor management committees can request payroll records and sue to enforce. The Division of Apprenticeship Standards handles apprenticeship violations. Penalties you should know Violation Law Penalty (per the statute) Paying less than prevailing wage Labor Code 1775 Up to $200 per worker per calendar day; minimums of $40, $80 for a repeat within 3 years, $120 if willful, plus the unpaid wages Not paying prevailing overtime Labor Code 1813 $25 per worker per day of violation Late or missing payroll records after a request Labor Code 1776 $100 per day per worker until produced Apprenticeship violations Labor Code 1777.7 Per day penalties, and debarment for serious violations Working or bidding unregistered Labor Code 1771.1 Penalties per day, up to a cap On top of these, liquidated damages equal to unpaid wages can apply if the wages aren't paid within the time allowed after an assessment. Repeated or willful violations can lead to debarment from public works for up to three years. The prime's responsibility The prime can be jointly liable for its subs' unpaid wages and some penalties, unless it took the steps the law describes to monitor them. Monitoring means: checking registration, collecting certified payroll, reviewing it, and acting on problems. If you receive an assessment There are short deadlines to request review. Call an attorney who handles prevailing wage cases the day it arrives.

items.s: The two bonds delivered after award: what each guarantees, the amounts, and who can make a claim.
items.x: In one sentence: the performance bond protects the agency if the work isn't finished, the payment bond protects the people who supplied labor and material if they aren't paid, and both are usually 100% of the contract. Payment bond Required on California public works contracts over $25,000 : Civil Code 9550 for local agencies, Public Contract Code 7103 for state entities. At least 100% of the contract price. Protects subcontractors, suppliers, workers and certain benefit funds and tax agencies that are owed money for the work. Claimants who don't have a direct contract with the prime must have given a 20 day preliminary notice (with exceptions for workers and certain funds). See stop payment notices. Performance bond Required by the contract, usually at 100% of the contract price. If the agency terminates you for default, the surety may finish the work, pay another contractor to finish it, or pay up to the bond amount. Delivering the bonds Bonds are due with the signed contract, on the agency's forms, from an admitted surety, with a power of attorney for the agent who signs. The agency must approve them before work starts. Change orders Bonds generally cover changes to the contract; large additions can raise the bonded amount and the premium. Keep your surety informed of major changes. PM notes A claim on your payment bond goes to your surety, who will ask you about it. Answer quickly and with documents; an unresolved bond claim affects your bonding capacity.

items.s: How monthly payments are measured and approved, how much retention can be held, and when it must be released.
items.x: In one sentence: on public works you're paid monthly for work in place, less retention of up to 5%, and the agency must release retention within a set time after completion. The monthly cycle 1. Measure quantities in place with the agency's inspector (unit price) or agree the percentage complete by item (lump sum, often from a schedule of values). 2. Progress estimate or pay application for the period, with any required supporting documents: certified payroll, updated schedule, material invoices for stored materials if allowed. 3. Agency review and approval by the engineer. 4. Payment within the time the contract and law allow. Local agencies must pay an undisputed, properly submitted request within 30 days (Public Contract Code 20104.50), or pay interest. Caltrans pays from monthly progress estimates under the Standard Specifications. Retention Under Public Contract Code 7201, retention on public works may not exceed 5% of each payment or of the contract price, unless the agency makes a finding, before bidding, that the project is substantially complex and states the higher amount in the bid documents. The prime can't withhold more from its subs than the agency withholds from it. You may usually substitute securities for retention or have it deposited in escrow (Public Contract Code 22300), if the contract allows. Release of retention Under Public Contract Code 7107, the agency must release retention within 60 days after completion of the work. It may withhold up to 150% of the value of disputed work. Late release carries interest. When you receive retention, pay each sub its share promptly (within 7 days under current law). PM notes Track quantities yourself every week, so the monthly estimate is a comparison, not a negotiation.

items.t: Paying subcontractors and suppliers on time
items.s: The prompt payment deadlines that apply to primes on California public works, and the penalties for paying late.
items.x: In one sentence: when the agency pays you, the clock starts on paying your subs: 7 days for progress payments under California law, unless the contract or a written agreement says otherwise. The deadlines Progress payments: a prime or sub must pay its subcontractors their share within 7 days of receiving each progress payment, unless otherwise agreed in writing (Business and Professions Code 7108.5 and the public contract equivalents). Retention: pay each sub its share within 7 days of receiving retention (Public Contract Code 7107). Suppliers: under the terms of your purchase order; federal aid contracts may set a deadline too. Withholding You may withhold from a sub when there's a good faith dispute, up to an amount related to the dispute. Withholding everything because of a small issue, or because the agency was late on an unrelated item, invites penalties. Penalties Late payment can cost 2% per month of the amount due, plus attorney's fees if the sub has to sue, and can be grounds for discipline by the CSLB. Federal aid reporting Federal aid jobs often require a monthly prompt payment certification listing every sub, at all tiers, and what was paid, even in months with no payment. See dbe requirements. PM notes Put the pay date for subs on the calendar the day the agency's payment lands, and keep the bank record. If you withhold, write to the sub the same day with the reason and the amount.

items.t: Getting paid: preliminary notices, stop payment notices and bond claims
items.s: Why there are no mechanics liens on public property, and how subs and suppliers protect their right to be paid on public works.
items.x: In one sentence: you can't put a lien on public property, so on public works the unpaid sub or supplier protects itself with a 20 day preliminary notice, then a stop payment notice on the agency's funds or a claim on the prime's payment bond. The 20 day preliminary notice If you don't have a direct contract with the prime (a lower tier sub, a supplier to a sub) you must give a preliminary notice to the agency, the prime and the surety if known. It protects your rights for work provided within 20 days before the notice and afterward, so send it within 20 days of first furnishing labor or material. Late is better than never: it still protects later work. Subs and suppliers with a direct contract with the prime generally don't need it for a stop payment notice, but many send it anyway. Stop payment notice A written notice to the agency that you're owed money. The agency must then withhold enough from the prime's payments to cover the claim. Timing: give it before the earlier of 30 days after a notice of completion or cessation is recorded , or 90 days after completion or cessation if none is recorded. A lawsuit to enforce it has its own deadline after that. Payment bond claim A claim on the prime's payment bond, to the surety and the prime. The preliminary notice keeps this right open. If you didn't give one, the Civil Code still lets you claim by written notice to the surety and the prime within 15 days after a notice of completion is recorded , or 75 days after completion if none is recorded (section 9560). A lawsuit on the bond must be filed within 6 months after the period for giving stop payment notices ends. Check the current Civil Code sections 9550–9566 for your situation. For primes When a stop payment notice is served on the agency, it holds your money. Resolve it with the claimant, or provide a release bond if the contract allows. Keep conditional and unconditional releases from every sub and supplier as you pay them. PM notes Ask the agency to tell you when it records the notice of completion. Every deadline in this article starts from it.

items.t: Claims and disputes on public contracts
items.s: How a disagreement becomes a claim, the Public Contract Code 9204 process and timelines, and what to document from day one.
items.x: In one sentence: most disputes are settled as change orders; when they aren't, the contract's notice and protest steps and the Public Contract Code 9204 claim process decide whether you get paid, so follow them exactly. Before a claim: notice and protest Almost every public contract requires prompt written notice when you believe something is extra work or a delay, and a written protest if the engineer disagrees. Caltrans' Standard Specifications set a detailed process and deadlines for this; local agencies have their own. Missing a notice deadline can waive the claim, however good it is. See change orders. Public Contract Code 9204 For California public works, PCC 9204 sets a claim process for a contractor's claim for time, payment or a disputed amount: 1. Submit the claim in writing by registered or certified mail, with reasonable documentation. 2. The agency reviews it and, within 45 days , provides a written statement of the disputed and undisputed portions. The period can be extended by mutual agreement. 3. The agency pays any undisputed portion within 60 days of its statement. 4. If you disagree, you may demand an informal meet and confer ; the agency schedules it within 30 days . 5. What remains disputed goes to nonbinding mediation , unless both sides agree otherwise. 6. Unpaid claim amounts accrue interest as the statute sets. A sub without a contract with the agency can ask the prime to present its claim; the prime must answer within 45 days whether it did. Documenting a claim Daily reports describing the issue as it happened. See daily reports. Photos with dates and locations. Labor, equipment and material records for the disputed work, kept separately. Correspondence and RFIs. A schedule analysis for delay: what was critical and why. PM notes Start a separate cost code the day something looks like extra work, even if you expect a quick change order.

items.t: Closeout, acceptance and the end of the job
items.s: Punch list, acceptance, the notice of completion, final payment, retention and the paperwork that keeps a job from staying open.
items.x: In one sentence: a public job is over when the agency accepts it and pays the final estimate and retention, and getting there is mostly paperwork you can start long before the last day of work. The steps 1. Punch list: the agency's list of items to finish or correct. Close it quickly; every week open costs overhead. 2. Acceptance: the agency formally accepts the work, often by action of its governing body for local agencies, or by the engineer's written acceptance on Caltrans jobs. See acceptance testing punch list. 3. Notice of completion: many agencies record one with the county recorder. It starts the deadlines for stop payment notices and bond claims. See stop payment notices. 4. Final estimate or final pay application , with all quantities agreed, change orders closed and claims either resolved or reserved in writing. 5. Release of retention within 60 days after completion, less up to 150% of disputed amounts. See progress payments retention. Paperwork that holds up final payment Certified payroll for every week, for every sub, including "no work" weeks. Apprenticeship records and training fund contributions. As built drawings and operation and maintenance manuals. See closeout package. Warranties and guarantees. Final DBE and prompt payment reports on federal aid jobs. Releases from subs and suppliers. After closeout Keep the job file for the record retention period in your contract and the law. Labor compliance audits and warranty claims can arrive after the job is closed. PM notes Start the closeout list at 75% complete. The documents you need from subs are easiest to get while they still want their own retention.
